Binned (classed) colour scales

Source: R/scales-binned.R
scale_fill_binned.Rd

scale_fill_binned() / scale_color_binned() cut a continuous aesthetic into classes and colour each class with one step of a sequential palette — the standard choropleth scale. By default the classes follow ggplot2's binning (style = "extended"): about n "nice" class boundaries inside the data range, the outer classes widened to whole bins, and classes closed on the right, (a, b]. A classification style chooses other breaks: quantile, equal, and pretty need no extra packages; other styles (e.g. "jenks", "fisher", "kmeans", "headtails") delegate to the optional classInt package (in Suggests) and error if it is absent. Those classes close on the left, [a, b).

The ggplot2-named binned colour scales follow ggplot2's binning: without breaks, about n.breaks "nice" class boundaries inside the data range, the outer classes widened to whole bins (with limits, the limits are the outer boundaries); classes close on the right, (a, b].

  • scale_*_steps() — a two-colour low–high ramp, each class taking the ramp's colour at its centre.

  • scale_*_steps2() — a diverging low–mid–high ramp centred on midpoint, each class taking the ramp's colour at its centre.

  • scale_*_stepsn() — an n-colour ramp colours, sampled at each class centre.

  • scale_*_fermenter() — a ColorBrewer palette's k-class colours (as scale_color_distiller(), but binned).

  • scale_*_viridis_b() — k evenly spaced viridis colours.

Usage

scale_fill_binned(
  plot,
  style = "extended",
  n = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  na_value = "grey80",
  name = NULL
)

scale_color_binned(
  plot,
  style = "extended",
  n = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  na_value = "grey80",
  name = NULL
)

scale_color_steps(
  plot,
  low = "#132B43",
  high = "#56B1F7",
  name = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  limits = NULL,
  n.breaks = NULL,
  na.value = "grey50",
  oob = NULL
)

  low = "#132B43",

  name = NULL,

Arguments

plot

A PlotSpec.

style

Classification style: "extended" (the default, ggplot2's breaks), "quantile", "equal", "pretty" (base R), or any classInt::classIntervals() style.

n

For "extended", the approximate number of class boundaries (default 5); for the other styles, the number of classes (default 5). Ignored when breaks is supplied.

breaks

Explicit class boundaries, overriding style/n. Under "extended" the data range is added as the outer boundaries (as ggplot2 adds its limits); under the other styles they are every boundary (length = number of classes + 1).

palette

A sequential palette: NULL (batlow), an grDevices::hcl.pals() name, or a vector of colours interpolated across the classes.

labels

Optional class labels (one per class); defaults to interval ranges like "(0, 10]".

na_value

Fill colour for NA values (shown as a distinct legend swatch). Default "grey80".

name

Legend title, or NULL to derive from the encoding.

low, mid, high, midpoint

For scale_*_steps(), the end colours low and high; for scale_*_steps2(), the end and midpoint colours and the data value at mid.

limits

For the ggplot2-named scales, a length-2 numeric c(min, max): the outer class boundaries.

n.breaks

For the ggplot2-named scales, the approximate number of class boundaries when breaks is NULL (default 5).

na.value

For the ggplot2-named scales, the colour of missing values.

oob

For the ggplot2-named scales, what to do with values outside the outer boundaries: "squish" (the default, as in ggplot2) colours them as the outer class, "censor" with na.value; or a function(x, range).

colours

For scale_*_stepsn(), the colours of the ramp.

values

For scale_*_stepsn(), the positions (between 0 and 1, one per colour, increasing) of colours along the ramp, or NULL to space them evenly.

type, direction

For scale_*_fermenter(), the ColorBrewer family a numeric palette indexes and its order (see scale_color_brewer()); for scale_*_viridis_b(), direction = -1 reverses the map.

option

For scale_*_viridis_b(), the viridis map (see scale_color_viridis_c()).

Value

The modified PlotSpec.

Details

A colour vector palette is a ramp, sampled at each class's centre as in ggplot2; a named palette (and the default) gives one evenly spaced colour per class.

See also

mark_sf(), scale_fill_continuous()

Examples

vplot(faithful) |>
  mark_point(x = eruptions, y = waiting, color = waiting) |>
  scale_color_binned()

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
vplot(nc) |>
  mark_sf(fill = SID74) |>
  scale_fill_binned(style = "quantile", n = 5) |>
  coord_sf()
} # }
vplot(faithful) |>
  mark_point(x = eruptions, y = waiting, color = waiting - 70) |>
  scale_color_steps2()
